sections.label: I
sections.title: Complete the sentences and match them to the pictures.
sections.note: Write an instrument, then choose its picture label. The letters a-c are picture labels only.

questions.prompt: 1. The ___ is a woodwind instrument that you may hear in a band or orchestra.

parts.label: Picture label
parts.explanation: The official answer is picture a for flute. A clarinet in picture b also fits the general description, so both are accepted when paired with the correct instrument word.

parts.label: Instrument
parts.explanation: The official answer is flute. Clarinet is also scientifically valid because it is a woodwind instrument that is played by blowing, so it is accepted too.

questions.prompt: 2. The ___ is a loud brass instrument that you hold in your lap to play.

parts.label: Instrument
parts.explanation: A tuba is a large brass instrument with a very low sound.

questions.prompt: 3. The ___ is a black woodwind instrument with a wooden reed at the end.

parts.label: Instrument
parts.explanation: A clarinet is usually black, is traditionally made of wood, and uses a single reed.

sections.label: J
sections.title: Write the words in the correct order.
sections.note: Use every word to make a complete sentence.

questions.prompt: 1. not / the tuba / as big as / The clarinet / is
answers: The clarinet is not as big as the tuba
The clarinet is not as big as the tuba.
questions.explanation: Use subject + is not as + adjective + as + comparison noun.

questions.prompt: 2. not as long as / The flute / the didgeridoo / is
answers: The flute is not as long as the didgeridoo
The flute is not as long as the didgeridoo.
questions.explanation: The complete comparison is The flute is not as long as the didgeridoo.

questions.prompt: 3. as difficult as / The erhu / the violin / is
answers: The erhu is as difficult as the violin
The erhu is as difficult as the violin.
questions.explanation: Use as + adjective + as to show that the difficulty is equal.

sections.label: K
sections.title: Look and complete the sentences.
sections.note: Use a comparison phrase from the box that matches each picture.

questions.prompt: 1. The erhu is ___ I am!
questions.explanation: The picture supports as big as or as tall as. The original answer key allows these comparison phrases to be interchanged when they match the picture.

questions.prompt: 2. Frederick is ___ our music teacher.
questions.explanation: The picture supports as tall as or as big as. The original answer key allows these comparison phrases to be interchanged when they match the picture.

questions.prompt: 3. The cello is ___ the violin.
questions.explanation: A cello is heavier than a violin, so it is not as light as the violin.

questions.prompt: 4. The drums are ___ the violin.
questions.explanation: The violin in the picture is older than the drums, so the drums are not as old as the violin.

sections.label: L
sections.title: Combine the sentences using as ... as or not as ... as.
sections.note: Write one complete comparison sentence without changing the meaning.

questions.prompt: 1. The violin is beautiful. The erhu is equally beautiful.
answers: The violin is as beautiful as the erhu
The violin is as beautiful as the erhu.
The erhu is as beautiful as the violin
The erhu is as beautiful as the violin.
questions.explanation: Both instruments are equally beautiful, so either subject order is correct with as beautiful as.

questions.prompt: 2. This tuba is more expensive than this cello.
answers: This cello is not as expensive as this tuba
This cello is not as expensive as this tuba.
This cello is not as expensive as the tuba
This cello is not as expensive as the tuba.
questions.explanation: If the tuba is more expensive, the cello is not as expensive as the tuba.

questions.prompt: 3. The panpipes are light. The flute is equally light.
answers: The panpipes are as light as the flute
The panpipes are as light as the flute.
The flute is as light as the panpipes
The flute is as light as the panpipes.
questions.explanation: Both instruments are equally light, so either subject order is correct with as light as.
